newsitem.title: USA: Special board meeting rumored at Westinghouse.
newsitem.headline: Special board meeting rumored at Westinghouse.

text.p: Wall Street analysts said Westinghouse Electric Corp was holding a special board meeting on Tuesday in New York to discuss the company's strategy for separating its broadcast and industrial businesses.
A company spokesman declined to confirm whether a meeting was scheduled. "We don't make public the board schedule of meetings," he said.
According to Nick Heymann at NatWest Securities, "sources inside the company" expected an unscheduled board meeting on Tuesday in New York.

"From what I've heard, today's meeting is to approve the blueprint of the spin-off," Heymann said. Westinghouse has said in recent weeks that it would announce its expected split strategy by year-end.
John Reidy, a media analyst at Smith Barney also said he'd heard of the meeting but had not confirmed it was taking place.
The company is separating its businesses to increase shareholder value.
Heymann said he asked Westinghouse about the meeting and its agenda, but the company would neither confirm nor deny to him that the meeting took place.

In a conference call on Monday, Westinghouse told analysts that an announcement about the split strategy would not be released for several weeks. The conference call took place after Westinghouse released third-quarter earnings.

Some analysts speculated recently that Westinghouse would not announce its split strategy until shareholders vote on its $3.9 billion purchase of radio giant Infinity Broadcasting, scheduled for December 10.
"They told us there would not be any formal announcement for several weeks," said Kent Newcomb at A.G. Edwards.
Heymann said he suspects Westinghouse will move fairly quickly on splitting its businesses, assuming the board gives the thumbs-up.
"It sounds to me like this isn't something that we'll hear about on December 15. It definitely appears to be on a more accelerated time frame," he said.

Heymann said his "best understanding" is the business split will structure Westinghouse into two completely separate corporations. He said the media business would wind up with much of the company's debt.
Analysts have also speculated recently that Westinghouse will announce after its split strategy that it is relocating its corporate headquarters to New York from Pittsburgh.
